Balanced-to-slightly positive interpretation: The FOMC notes strong Q3 growth and a still-tight labor market but acknowledges elevated inflation and tighter credit—an approach consistent with Taylor-rule prescriptions and estimated policy rules (Taylor; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) that call for maintaining restrictive rates when inflation is above target. The focus on cumulative tightening and policy lags mirrors the monetary transmission literature (e.g., Bernanke–Mihov) and recognizes short-run Phillips-curve trade-offs between inflation and employment. Continuing QT via Treasuries and agency MBS reduces reserves (nonborrowed-reserves channel), reinforcing restraint, while describing the banking system as sound limits perceived fragility and moral-hazard concerns. Forward-looking monitoring and readiness to adjust are in line with flexible inflation targeting and managing expectations. Net tone: cautious yet mildly positive on current activity, tempered by inflation risks.
